27logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

29# The forward accumulates the log-sum-exp ``M`` in log2 base, while the 

30# backward expects a natural-log base ``L``. Convert at the boundary so the 

31# autograd-saved LSE is numerically correct. 

32_LN2 = math.log(2.0) 

33 

34# Dropout is currently forced to 0.0 (see assert below), so the philox RNG 

35# state returned to autograd is never consumed by the backward pass 

36# (`_parse_philox` is only called when `is_dropout` is True). Returning GPU 

37# tensors here would add two `cudaMalloc` calls per forward for no benefit. 

38# Use cheap CPU constants; restore as GPU tensors carrying the real RNG 

39# state once dropout is actually supported. 

40_PHILOX_SEED = torch.tensor(0, dtype=torch.long) 

41_PHILOX_OFFSET = torch.tensor(0, dtype=torch.long) 

42 

43# The fast paths below only touch the usual float dtypes; anything more 

44# exotic (fp8, integer views, ...) falls back to the shared generic path. 

45_FAST_DTYPES = (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16, torch.float32)

48@triton.jit 

49def _eff_attn_step( 

50 acc, 

51 p_sum, 

52 query, 

53 k_base, 

54 v_base, 

55 offs_m, 

56 offs_d, 

57 start_n, 

58 stride_k_seqlen, 

59 stride_k_headsize, 

60 stride_v_seqlen, 

61 stride_v_headsize, 

62 qk_scale_log2e, 

63 BLOCK_N: tl.constexpr, 

64 MASKED: tl.constexpr, 

65): 

66 offs_n = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_N) 

67 pos = start_n + offs_n 

68 key = tl.load( 

69 k_base + offs_d[:, None] * stride_k_headsize + pos[None, :] * stride_k_seqlen 

70 ) 

71 # Issue the V load together with K: both DMAs are independent of the 

72 # QK dot, so overlapping them cuts the per-program serial latency on 

73 # the single-KV-block shapes this path serves. 

74 value = tl.load( 

75 v_base + pos[:, None] * stride_v_seqlen + offs_d[None, :] * stride_v_headsize 

76 ) 

77 qk = tl.dot(query, key, allow_tf32=False) 

78 # Scale in fp32 after the dot: pre-scaling Q and casting it back to a 

79 # 16-bit dtype (the shared no-max kernel's trick for wide tiles) loses 

80 # ~2e-3 relative accuracy per Q element, which pushes a few outputs of 

81 # the small shapes past the efficient-attention tolerance. 

82 qk = qk * qk_scale_log2e 

83 if MASKED: 

84 # Additive mask in the style of the generic kernel: exp2(-30000) 

85 # underflows to exactly zero. Selecting -inf on the scaled dot 

86 # output instead miscompiles occasionally on these tiles (a 

87 # rare-element accuracy drift against the reference). 

88 qk = qk + tl.where(offs_m[:, None] >= pos[None, :], 0.0, -30000.0) 

89 p = tl.math.exp2(qk) 

90 p_sum = p_sum + p 

91 # Keep p in fp32 and widen V instead: casting p to a 16-bit dtype 

92 # before the PV dot is the second accuracy leak of the shared kernel. 

93 acc = tl.dot(p, value.to(tl.float32), acc, allow_tf32=False) 

94 return acc, p_sum

97@triton.jit 

98def _eff_attn_fwd( 

99 Q, 

100 K, 

101 V, 

102 M, 

103 Out, 

104 sm_scale, 

105 stride_q_batch, 

106 stride_q_head, 

107 stride_q_seqlen, 

108 stride_q_headsize, 

109 stride_k_batch, 

110 stride_k_head, 

111 stride_k_seqlen, 

112 stride_k_headsize, 

113 stride_v_batch, 

114 stride_v_head, 

115 stride_v_seqlen, 

116 stride_v_headsize, 

117 stride_o_batch, 

118 stride_o_head, 

119 stride_o_seqlen, 

120 stride_o_headsize, 

121 q_head_num, 

122 Q_CTX, 

123 KV_CTX, 

124 HEAD_DIM: tl.constexpr, 

125 BLOCK_M: tl.constexpr, 

126 BLOCK_N: tl.constexpr, 

127 CAUSAL: tl.constexpr, 

128): 

129 # No-max flash forward for small shapes (all fast dtypes, causal 

130 # included); see `_eff_attn_step` for the two fp32-accuracy fixes 

131 # versus the shared `_attn_fwd_nomax` (which keeps serving fp32 

132 # inputs, where its casts are exact). 

133 start_m = tl.program_id(0) 

134 off_hz = tl.program_id(1) 

135 batch_id = off_hz // q_head_num 

136 head_id = off_hz % q_head_num 

137 

138 q_offset = ( 

139 batch_id.to(tl.int64) * stride_q_batch + head_id.to(tl.int64) * stride_q_head 

140 ) 

141 o_offset = ( 

142 batch_id.to(tl.int64) * stride_o_batch + head_id.to(tl.int64) * stride_o_head 

143 ) 

144 kv_offset = ( 

145 batch_id.to(tl.int64) * stride_k_batch + head_id.to(tl.int64) * stride_k_head 

146 ) 

147 

148 offs_m = start_m * BLOCK_M + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_M) 

149 offs_d = tl.arange(0, HEAD_DIM) 

150 

151 # Every load here is unmasked; the host dispatches only when Q_CTX and 

152 # KV_CTX are multiples of the block sizes. 

153 query = tl.load( 

154 Q 

155 + q_offset 

156 + offs_m[:, None] * stride_q_seqlen 

157 + offs_d[None, :] * stride_q_headsize 

158 ) 

159 qk_scale_log2e = sm_scale * 1.4426950408889634 

160 

161 k_base = K + kv_offset 

162 v_base = V + kv_offset 

163 

164 p_sum = tl.zeros([BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N], dtype=tl.float32) 

165 acc = tl.zeros([BLOCK_M, HEAD_DIM], dtype=tl.float32) 

166 if CAUSAL: 

167 # Off-band: everything strictly above the diagonal block is unmasked. 

168 # Requires BLOCK_M % BLOCK_N == 0 so the split points are block 

169 # aligned. The `start_m > 0` guard matters: for row block 0 this 

170 # range is empty, and a 0-trip version of the loop miscompiles on 

171 # GCU400 (same caveat as the shared kernel). 

172 if start_m > 0: 

173 for start_n in tl.range(0, start_m * BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N): 

174 acc, p_sum = _eff_attn_step( 

175 acc, 

176 p_sum, 

177 query, 

178 k_base, 

179 v_base, 

180 offs_m, 

181 offs_d, 

182 start_n, 

183 stride_k_seqlen, 

184 stride_k_headsize, 

185 stride_v_seqlen, 

186 stride_v_headsize, 

187 qk_scale_log2e, 

188 BLOCK_N, 

189 MASKED=False, 

190 ) 

191 # On-band: only the BLOCK_M/BLOCK_N blocks touching the diagonal. 

192 for start_n in tl.range(start_m * BLOCK_M, (start_m + 1) * BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N): 

193 acc, p_sum = _eff_attn_step( 

194 acc, 

195 p_sum, 

196 query, 

197 k_base, 

198 v_base, 

199 offs_m, 

200 offs_d, 

201 start_n, 

202 stride_k_seqlen, 

203 stride_k_headsize, 

204 stride_v_seqlen, 

205 stride_v_headsize, 

206 qk_scale_log2e, 

207 BLOCK_N, 

208 MASKED=True, 

209 ) 

210 else: 

211 for start_n in tl.range(0, KV_CTX, BLOCK_N): 

212 acc, p_sum = _eff_attn_step( 

213 acc, 

214 p_sum, 

215 query, 

216 k_base, 

217 v_base, 

218 offs_m, 

219 offs_d, 

220 start_n, 

221 stride_k_seqlen, 

222 stride_k_headsize, 

223 stride_v_seqlen, 

224 stride_v_headsize, 

225 qk_scale_log2e, 

226 BLOCK_N, 

227 MASKED=False, 

228 ) 

229 

230 l_i = tl.sum(p_sum, 1) 

231 acc = acc / l_i[:, None] 

232 tl.store( 

233 Out 

234 + o_offset 

235 + offs_m[:, None] * stride_o_seqlen 

236 + offs_d[None, :] * stride_o_headsize, 

237 acc.to(Out.dtype.element_ty), 

238 ) 

239 # LSE in the natural-log base, matching aten's log_sumexp contract. 

240 lse_row = tl.math.log2(l_i) * 0.6931471805599453 

241 tl.store(M + off_hz * Q_CTX + offs_m, lse_row)

244@triton.jit 

245def _eff_attn_tiny_fwd( 

246 Q, 

247 K, 

248 V, 

249 M, 

250 Out, 

251 sm_scale, 

252 stride_q_batch, 

253 stride_q_head, 

254 stride_q_seqlen, 

255 stride_q_headsize, 

256 stride_k_batch, 

257 stride_k_head, 

258 stride_k_seqlen, 

259 stride_k_headsize, 

260 stride_v_batch, 

261 stride_v_head, 

262 stride_v_seqlen, 

263 stride_v_headsize, 

264 stride_o_batch, 

265 stride_o_head, 

266 stride_o_seqlen, 

267 stride_o_headsize, 

268 q_head_num, 

269 Q_CTX, 

270 KV_CTX, 

271 HEAD_DIM: tl.constexpr, 

272 BLOCK_M: tl.constexpr, 

273 BLOCK_N: tl.constexpr, 

274 CAUSAL: tl.constexpr, 

275): 

276 # Latency path for very short sequences (Q_CTX/KV_CTX < 16, tl.dot's 

277 # minimum tile): one program per (batch, head) computes the whole head 

278 # with broadcast-sum "matmuls". Scores are kept in the log2 domain with 

279 # no running max, matching `_attn_fwd_nomax`'s exactness argument. 

280 pid = tl.program_id(0) 

281 batch_id = pid // q_head_num 

282 head_id = pid % q_head_num 

283 q_off = ( 

284 batch_id.to(tl.int64) * stride_q_batch + head_id.to(tl.int64) * stride_q_head 

285 ) 

286 o_off = ( 

287 batch_id.to(tl.int64) * stride_o_batch + head_id.to(tl.int64) * stride_o_head 

288 ) 

289 kv_off = ( 

290 batch_id.to(tl.int64) * stride_k_batch + head_id.to(tl.int64) * stride_k_head 

291 ) 

292 

293 offs_m = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_M) 

294 offs_n = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_N) 

295 offs_d = tl.arange(0, HEAD_DIM) 

296 m_ok = offs_m < Q_CTX 

297 n_ok = offs_n < KV_CTX 

298 

299 q = tl.load( 

300 Q 

301 + q_off 

302 + offs_m[:, None] * stride_q_seqlen 

303 + offs_d[None, :] * stride_q_headsize, 

304 mask=m_ok[:, None], 

305 other=0.0, 

306 ) 

307 k = tl.load( 

308 K 

309 + kv_off 

310 + offs_n[:, None] * stride_k_seqlen 

311 + offs_d[None, :] * stride_k_headsize, 

312 mask=n_ok[:, None], 

313 other=0.0, 

314 ) 

315 # Hoisted next to the K load: V is independent of the scores, so the 

316 # two DMAs overlap and the per-program serial latency shrinks. 

317 v = tl.load( 

318 V 

319 + kv_off 

320 + offs_n[:, None] * stride_v_seqlen 

321 + offs_d[None, :] * stride_v_headsize, 

322 mask=n_ok[:, None], 

323 other=0.0, 

324 ) 

325 qf = q.to(tl.float32) * (sm_scale * 1.4426950408889634) 

326 scores = tl.sum(qf[:, None, :] * k.to(tl.float32)[None, :, :], 2) 

327 # exp2(-inf) == 0 kills padded columns exactly, so the deferred row sum 

328 # stays exact for both the causal and the padded-column case. 

329 if CAUSAL: 

330 keep = (offs_m[:, None] >= offs_n[None, :]) & n_ok[None, :] 

331 else: 

332 keep = n_ok[None, :] 

333 scores = tl.where(keep, scores, -float("inf")) 

334 p = tl.math.exp2(scores) 

335 l_i = tl.sum(p, 1) 

336 acc = tl.sum(p[:, :, None] * v.to(tl.float32)[None, :, :], 1) 

337 acc = acc / l_i[:, None] 

338 tl.store( 

339 Out 

340 + o_off 

341 + offs_m[:, None] * stride_o_seqlen 

342 + offs_d[None, :] * stride_o_headsize, 

343 acc.to(Out.dtype.element_ty), 

344 mask=m_ok[:, None], 

345 ) 

346 # LSE in the natural-log base, matching aten's log_sumexp contract. 

347 lse_row = tl.math.log2(l_i) * 0.6931471805599453 

348 tl.store(M + pid * Q_CTX + offs_m, lse_row, mask=m_ok) 

349 

350 

351def _next_pow2(n): 

352 return 1 << max(0, (n - 1).bit_length())

354 

355def _scaled_dot_product_efficient_attention( 

356 query, 

357 key, 

358 value, 

359 attn_bias=None, 

360 compute_log_sumexp=False, 

361 dropout_p=0.0, 

362 is_causal=False, 

363 scale=None, 

364): 

365 """Implements scaled dot product attention with efficient memory usage. 

366 

367 Args: 

368 query: (batch, num_heads, seq_len_q, head_dim) 

369 key: (batch, num_kv_heads, seq_len_kv, head_dim) 

370 value: (batch, num_kv_heads, seq_len_kv, head_dim) 

371 attn_bias: optional attention bias 

372 compute_log_sumexp: currently ignored; the log_sumexp (``M``) is 

373 always computed and returned by ``scaled_dot_product_attention_forward``. 

374 A future optimization can plumb this flag into the forward kernel 

375 to skip allocating ``M`` when the backward does not need it. 

376 dropout_p: dropout probability (currently must be 0.0) 

377 is_causal: whether to use causal masking 

378 scale: optional scale factor 

379 

380 Returns: 

381 output: (batch, num_heads, seq_len_q, head_dim) 

382 log_sumexp: (batch, num_heads, seq_len_q) in natural-log base, the 

383 forward kernel's ``M`` converted from log2 base (the 

384 ``compute_log_sumexp`` flag is currently a no-op). 

385 philox_seed: random seed for dropout (placeholder until dropout is supported) 

386 philox_offset: random offset for dropout (placeholder until dropout is supported) 

387 """ 

388 logger.debug("GEMS_ENFLAME_GCU400 SCALED_DOT_PRODUCT_EFFICIENT_ATTENTION") 

389 

390 assert dropout_p == 0.0, "Currently only support dropout_p=0.0" 

391 

392 # Fast path: launch a GCU400-tuned no-max kernel directly and let it 

393 # emit the log-sum-exp in the natural-log base. This keeps the whole op 

394 # a single kernel launch with a lean Python wrapper; the shared forward 

395 # plus a separate aten multiply used to cost one extra device kernel 

396 # and ~25us of host time per call. 

397 if ( 

398 attn_bias is None 

399 and query.dim() == 4 

400 and query.dtype in _FAST_DTYPES 

401 and key.dtype == query.dtype 

402 and value.dtype == query.dtype 

403 ): 

404 batch, q_heads, q_ctx, head_dim = query.shape 

405 kv_heads = key.shape[1] 

406 kv_ctx = key.shape[2] 

407 if head_dim in (16, 32, 64, 128) and q_heads == kv_heads and q_ctx == kv_ctx: 

408 sm_scale = scale if scale is not None else 1.0 / (head_dim**0.5) 

409 block_m, block_n, num_warps = _nomax_launch_config(q_ctx, kv_ctx) 

410 divisible = ( 

411 q_ctx % block_m == 0 

412 and kv_ctx % block_n == 0 

413 and (not is_causal or block_m % block_n == 0) 

414 ) 

415 # Dispatch: small divisible shapes (q_ctx <= 128) take 

416 # `_eff_attn_fwd`, whose exact fp32 pipeline (post-dot scale, 

417 # fp32 p and V through the PV dot) tracks the native sdpa 

418 # reference inside the 2e-3 tolerance. Causal 16-bit used to 

419 # fall back to the generic path because the native causal PV 

420 # stage itself then drifted ~2.5e-3 from the fp64 truth, and 

421 # only the generic kernel's matching rounding tracked it; 

422 # that premise is stale (2026-11-13: the native reference 

423 # sits ~1e-5 from fp64 truth while the generic path's 16-bit 

424 # rounding — Q pre-scale cast + p down-cast — drifts ~2.5e-3, 

425 # failing the accuracy gate on ~1/3 of random trials). 

426 # fp32 keeps the shared kernel for wider sequences (its casts 

427 # are exact there). 

428 use_eff = divisible and q_ctx <= 128 

429 use_shared = divisible and not use_eff and query.dtype == torch.float32 

430 if use_eff or use_shared: 

431 o = torch.empty_like(query, dtype=value.dtype) 

432 m = torch.empty( 

433 (batch, q_heads, q_ctx), device=query.device, dtype=torch.float32 

434 ) 

435 grid = (q_ctx // block_m, batch * q_heads) 

436 strides = ( 

437 query.stride(0), 

438 query.stride(1), 

439 query.stride(2), 

440 query.stride(3), 

441 key.stride(0), 

442 key.stride(1), 

443 key.stride(2), 

444 key.stride(3), 

445 value.stride(0), 

446 value.stride(1), 

447 value.stride(2), 

448 value.stride(3), 

449 o.stride(0), 

450 o.stride(1), 

451 o.stride(2), 

452 o.stride(3), 

453 ) 

454 if use_shared: 

455 _attn_fwd_nomax[grid]( 

456 query, 

457 key, 

458 value, 

459 m, 

460 o, 

461 sm_scale, 

462 *strides, 

463 q_heads, 

464 q_ctx, 

465 kv_ctx, 

466 HEAD_DIM=head_dim, 

467 BLOCK_M=block_m, 

468 BLOCK_N=block_n, 

469 DEFER_SUM=True, 

470 CAUSAL=is_causal, 

471 LSE_BASE_E=True, 

472 num_warps=num_warps, 

473 num_stages=2, 

474 ) 

475 else: 

476 # num_warps=1 measured fastest on the small tiles this 

477 # path serves (<= 64x64); keep the family default (2) 

478 # for the wider D=128 tiles. 

479 eff_num_warps = 1 if head_dim <= 64 else num_warps 

480 _eff_attn_fwd[grid]( 

481 query, 

482 key, 

483 value, 

484 m, 

485 o, 

486 sm_scale, 

487 *strides, 

488 q_heads, 

489 q_ctx, 

490 kv_ctx, 

491 HEAD_DIM=head_dim, 

492 BLOCK_M=block_m, 

493 BLOCK_N=block_n, 

494 CAUSAL=is_causal, 

495 num_warps=eff_num_warps, 

496 num_stages=2, 

497 ) 

498 return o, m, _PHILOX_SEED, _PHILOX_OFFSET 

499 if ( 

500 q_ctx <= 16 

501 and kv_ctx <= 16 

502 and head_dim in (16, 32, 64) 

503 and value.shape[2] == kv_ctx 

504 ): 

505 o = torch.empty_like(query, dtype=value.dtype) 

506 m = torch.empty( 

507 (batch, q_heads, q_ctx), device=query.device, dtype=torch.float32 

508 ) 

509 _eff_attn_tiny_fwd[(batch * q_heads,)]( 

510 query, 

511 key, 

512 value, 

513 m, 

514 o, 

515 sm_scale, 

516 query.stride(0), 

517 query.stride(1), 

518 query.stride(2), 

519 query.stride(3), 

520 key.stride(0), 

521 key.stride(1), 

522 key.stride(2), 

523 key.stride(3), 

524 value.stride(0), 

525 value.stride(1), 

526 value.stride(2), 

527 value.stride(3), 

528 o.stride(0), 

529 o.stride(1), 

530 o.stride(2), 

531 o.stride(3), 

532 q_heads, 

533 q_ctx, 

534 kv_ctx, 

535 HEAD_DIM=head_dim, 

536 BLOCK_M=_next_pow2(q_ctx), 

537 BLOCK_N=_next_pow2(kv_ctx), 

538 CAUSAL=is_causal, 

539 num_warps=2, 

540 num_stages=1, 

541 ) 

542 return o, m, _PHILOX_SEED, _PHILOX_OFFSET 

543 

544 # ``M`` (log_sumexp) is unconditionally computed inside 

545 # ``scaled_dot_product_attention_forward``; the ``compute_log_sumexp`` 

546 # flag is currently a no-op. Convert ``M`` from log2 base to natural-log 

547 # base (multiply by ln(2)) so the autograd-saved LSE is numerically correct. 

548 output, m = scaled_dot_product_attention_forward( 

549 query, 

550 key, 

551 value, 

552 attn_bias, 

553 dropout_p, 

554 is_causal, 

555 scale, 

556 enable_gqa=False, 

557 ) 

558 

559 log_sumexp = m * _LN2 

560 

561 return output, log_sumexp, _PHILOX_SEED, _PHILOX_OFFSET 

562 

563 

564def _efficient_attention_forward( 

565 query, 

566 key, 

567 value, 

568 bias=None, 

569 cu_seqlens_q=None, 

570 cu_seqlens_k=None, 

571 max_seqlen_q=None, 

572 max_seqlen_k=None, 

573 dropout_p=0.0, 

574 custom_mask_type=0, 

575 compute_log_sumexp=False, 

576 *, 

577 scale=None, 

578 seqlen_k=None, 

579 window_size=None, 

580): 

581 """aten ``_efficient_attention_forward`` (memory-efficient SDPA) entry. 

582 

583 The aten op is BSHD-native (cutlass/xformers layout): query (B, Sq, H, D), 

584 key/value (B, Sk, Hkv, D), bias (B, H, Sq, Sk); the efficient forward above 

585 is BHSD-native, so the tensors enter as transpose views (the kernels index 

586 through raw strides, no copy) and the output is transposed back. The 

587 logsumexp contract is (B, H, Sq) in the natural-log base, which the 

588 efficient forward already emits. 

589 """ 

590 logger.debug("GEMS_ENFLAME_GCU400 _EFFICIENT_ATTENTION_FORWARD") 

591 

592 if cu_seqlens_q is not None or cu_seqlens_k is not None: 

593 raise NotImplementedError( 

594 "_efficient_attention_forward: varlen is not supported" 

595 ) 

596 if custom_mask_type not in (0, 1): 

597 raise NotImplementedError( 

598 f"_efficient_attention_forward: custom_mask_type {custom_mask_type}" 

599 " is not supported" 

600 ) 

601 if window_size is not None and window_size >= 0: 

602 raise NotImplementedError( 

603 "_efficient_attention_forward: window_size is not supported" 

604 ) 

605 

606 ( 

607 output_bh, 

608 log_sumexp, 

609 philox_seed, 

610 philox_offset, 

611 ) = _scaled_dot_product_efficient_attention( 

612 query.transpose(1, 2), 

613 key.transpose(1, 2), 

614 value.transpose(1, 2), 

615 attn_bias=bias, 

616 compute_log_sumexp=compute_log_sumexp, 

617 dropout_p=dropout_p, 

618 is_causal=custom_mask_type == 1, 

619 scale=scale, 

620 ) 

621 

622 return ( 

623 output_bh.transpose(1, 2), 

624 log_sumexp, 

625 philox_seed, 

626 philox_offset, 

627 query.shape[1], 

628 key.shape[1], 

629 ) 

630 

631 

632# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

633# torch_gcu dispatch adaptation (aten::_efficient_attention_forward has no GCU kernel) 

634# 

635# torch_gcu only registers a CPU fallback for this op (aten_cpu_fallback [backend fallback]); 

636# calling with GCU tensors moves them to CPU and then raises NotImplementedError - the accuracy framework and 

637# The benchmark reference leg calls torch.ops.aten.* directly without enable()/use_gems(); efficient 

638# family's forward reference legs (tests/test_flash_attention_backward.py etc.) all fail. 

639# Following the existing pattern in `resize_as_sparse_.py` / `_flash_attention_forward.py`, register this 

640# implementation idempotently on the device key: an explicit kernel outranks the backend fallback and 

641# takes effect on import flag_gems; later duplicate registration of the same key by enable()/use_gems() is 

642# caught by the registrar as a warning and registers the same function, so behavior is unchanged. 

643# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

644_EFF_ATTN_FWD_KEY_FLAG = "_flag_gems_gcu400_eff_attn_fwd_key_registered" 

645_EFF_ATTN_FWD_LIBRARY = None 

646 

647 

648def _ensure_eff_attn_fwd_key_registration(): 

649 global _EFF_ATTN_FWD_LIBRARY 

650 if getattr(torch, _EFF_ATTN_FWD_KEY_FLAG, False): 

651 return 

652 _EFF_ATTN_FWD_LIBRARY = torch.library.Library("aten", "IMPL") 

653 try: 

654 _EFF_ATTN_FWD_LIBRARY.impl( 

655 "_efficient_attention_forward", 

656 _efficient_attention_forward, 

657 runtime.device.dispatch_key, 

658 ) 

659 except RuntimeError as error: 

660 logger.warning( 

661 "_efficient_attention_forward device-key registration skipped: %s", 

662 error, 

663 ) 

664 setattr(torch, _EFF_ATTN_FWD_KEY_FLAG, True) 

665 

666 

667_ensure_eff_attn_fwd_key_registration()
